string.text: Concrete Foundation

A cast concrete slab one building tile across, edged with steel angle and anchor bolts. It stands 40 cm proud of the ground and its deep skirt hides uneven terrain. Walls, floors and stairs snap onto it, and further foundations snap alongside.
Plank Floor
Floorboards nailed over joists, one building tile across. Snaps beside other floors and foundations, or on top of walls to start the next storey; the joists underneath make the ceiling below.
Plank Wall with Window
A plank wall the same size as the Hideout Furniture walls, with a four-pane window and a pair of shutters. Snaps to floor and foundation edges, beside other walls and on top of them.
Plank Gable Wall
A triangular plank wall that sits on top of a wall and closes the open end under a sloped, hip or valley roof. Press R while placing to flip which end is high.
Wooden Stairs
A wooden stair run with handrails that climbs exactly one storey over one building tile. Snaps onto floors and foundations.
Flat Tin Roof
Rusted corrugated sheets on timber rafters, one building tile across. Snaps on top of walls and beside other flat roofs.
Sloped Tin Roof
A 30 degree corrugated tin roof that rises one storey across one building tile. Snaps along wall tops and beside other sloped roofs; close the open sides with gable walls.
Tin Roof Outer Corner
A hip corner for the sloped tin roof: two slopes meeting on a diagonal ridge. Four of them over a 2x2 building make a pyramid roof.
Tin Roof Inner Corner
A valley corner for the sloped tin roof, joining two slopes at an inside corner with a steel valley flashing.
Pyramid Tin Roof
A four-sided tin roof cap for a one-tile building, with eaves all round and a steel finial at the peak. Snaps on top of the walls.
Low Plank Wall
A waist-high plank wall, one building tile wide, with a capping rail. Snaps to floor and foundation edges. Nothing stacks on top of it.
Plank Wall with Loophole
A full-height plank wall with a narrow firing slit. Snaps to floor and foundation edges, beside other walls and on top of them.
Wide Plank Doorway
A plank wall with a wide double-door opening and a lintel. Snaps to floor and foundation edges, beside other walls and on top of them.
Wooden Support Post
A square timber post with a base block and capital. Snaps to the corners of floors and foundations and holds up the storey above.
Triangular Plank Floor
Half a plank floor tile cut along the diagonal. Snaps to floors and foundations in any of the four orientations, or against a matching triangle to complete a full tile.
Triangular Concrete Foundation
Half a concrete foundation tile cut along the diagonal. Snaps to foundations in any of the four orientations, or against a matching triangle to complete a full tile.
Plank Entry Steps
Three wide steps up to the height of a foundation. Snaps to the outside edge of a foundation.
Plank Ramp
A long plank ramp that climbs one storey across a tile, open underneath. Snaps onto floors and foundations like the stairs.
L-Shaped Wooden Stairs
Stairs that turn a corner on a landing, open underneath, climbing one storey inside one tile. Snaps onto floors and foundations; press R to turn.
L-Shaped Wooden Stairs (Mirrored)
The mirror image of the L-shaped stairs, turning the other way. Snaps onto floors and foundations; press R to turn.
U-Shaped Wooden Stairs
Two flights joined by a landing, open underneath, climbing one storey inside one tile. Snaps onto floors and foundations; press R to turn.
Wooden Spiral Stairs
Treads winding round a central column, climbing one storey inside one tile. Snaps onto floors and foundations.
Triangular Tin Roof
Half a flat tin roof tile cut along the diagonal. Snaps on top of walls in any of the four orientations, or against a matching triangle or flat roof to complete a tile.
Plank Floor with Spiral Opening
A plank floor tile with a round opening and a railing, for the top of the spiral stairs. Snaps like a floor: beside floors and foundations, or on top of walls.
